notes.general_comments:
Three of the four candidates who took this paper did remarkably well. One managed to answer 28 out of the
30 questions correctly, and two others each produced 25 correct answers. With just 4 candidates, it would
not be appropriate or meaningful to subject each of the individual items to the statistical tests normally
applied to multiple choice papers. Suffice it to say that none of the 30 items were answered incorrectly by all
4 candidates, and, indeed, there was only one item, Question 18, which was answered incorrectly by 3 of
the candidates. There were a further 8 items which were answered correctly by two out of the four
candidates. In the case of one of these items, Question 25, two of the candidates who performed well on
the paper overall failed to work out which was the correct response.
